scoring: Answer key for comparing Vista (LLM review) with Prowler (rule-based scanner). It holds facts and published AWS Security Hub FSBP control severities only; it contains no ratings of its own. A tool's output is matched to a scenario by the identifier in terraform output scenario_resources (the instance ID). condition flaw: reporting the scenario counts as a detection. condition flaw_blocked: a misconfiguration is present but another deployed control removes the path it opens; reporting it is shown as a separate report rate, counted as neither a detection nor a false positive. condition hardened: no misconfiguration was planted; reporting it is a false positive. fsbp lists the FSBP controls that fail because of the scenario's configuration: a setting in which the scenario differs from its module's hardened default, or a resource its configuration associates with it (its security groups, its subnet's network ACL, its IAM role, and the load balancer, listeners, and target group it is registered with). fsbp_severity is the highest published severity in that list. On coverage fsbp scenarios the reported severity (NONE when the scenario is not reported) is compared with fsbp_severity on the order NONE < LOW < MEDIUM < HIGH < CRITICAL; outside_fsbp scenarios are scored for detection and false positives only. Controls in baseline_controls fail regardless of scenario and are in no scenario's fsbp. scripts/score.py applies these rules.

baseline_controls.note: FSBP controls known to fail regardless of scenario, for example account-level settings, the VPCs the scenario resources run in, settings left at the module's hardened default that every scenario starts from, and deletion protection, which every resource leaves off so one terraform destroy removes everything. The list is not exhaustive: other FSBP controls can also fail regardless of scenario, depending on account settings at scan time. They are in no scenario's fsbp list. Backing resources no scenario is scored on (for example the S3 access-log bucket, the DynamoDB table, the SQS queue, the KMS key) are not evaluated here.

scenarios.title: Storefront behind an internet-facing HTTPS load balancer
scenarios.description: Private instance with no public IP, IMDSv2 required, an encrypted root volume, the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy, and the node-exporter security group (TCP 9100 from the VPC CIDR 10.80.0.0/16); it accepts TCP 8080 only from the load balancer's security group and is the target of the default action of the HTTPS:443 listener on the internet-facing Application Load Balancer, which also has an HTTP:80 listener that redirects to HTTPS.
